$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. DeviceIdentity per FB-RAT-DEV-002 (device object model). Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<DeviceIdentity> (see schemas/common/envelope.schema.json), inheriting schemaVersion/producer/createdAtUtc from that outer envelope; `deviceIdentityId` below is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID, distinct from the envelope's objectId — a device keeps the same deviceIdentityId across reconnects, USB-port moves, and re-enumeration.
title: DeviceIdentity
description: What a discovered device claims to be: USB family classification, board reference (via Arduino CLI/PlatformIO metadata per FB-RAT-DEV-009, never a separate owned board catalog), MCU, USB descriptor, serial number, bootloader entry method, capabilities, and — load-bearing per FB-RAT-DEV-004 — an explicit identification-confidence claim a flash preflight gates on. See docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §2.

deviceIdentityId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this device (FB-RAT-COM-002), independent of USB port, transportPath, or displayName — the same physical board keeps this id across unplug/replug and even across a firmware re-flash that changes its USB descriptor strings.

mcu.description: Free-string MCU identifier when known, e.g. 'ATmega328P', 'ESP32-S3', 'RP2040'. Null when discovery has not yet determined it (e.g. mid-handshake, or a family/board pairing where the MCU is ambiguous without a further probe).

usbDescriptor.description: Raw USB vendor/product identification, when the device was discovered over USB (all nine FB-RAT-DEV-010 families are). Null only transiently, before Android's UsbManager enumeration has completed for this device.

serial.description: The device's OWN USB serial-number string (iSerialNumber), when it reports one — distinct from `deviceIdentityId`, which this constellation generates and owns. Many CH34x/inexpensive CP210x clones report no serial at all (null is common and expected, not an error) — this is exactly why `deviceIdentityId` cannot simply BE the USB serial and must be independently assigned.

bootloaderInfo.description: How this identity's board enters/speaks a bootloader protocol, when applicable. Null for a device with no known bootloader path (e.g. a CDC-only serial peripheral this constellation only ever talks to, never flashes).

capabilities.description: Optional CapabilityManifest (reused from schemas/common/capability-manifest.schema.json, not redefined here) narrowed to subjectKind='DEVICE' — which device.* operations (serial, flash, debug, self-test) this identity currently claims support for. Null before a capability handshake has completed.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

UsbFamily.description: FB-RAT-DEV-010 (EXPERIMENTAL — cross-reference docs/non_ratified/EXPERIMENTAL_DECISIONS.md): the nine-family initial USB target matrix. This field records which family the device was DISCOVERED/CLASSIFIED under, not an exhaustive claim about every protocol the physical board might also speak — a board can legitimately present as CDC while running an STK500-speaking bootloader underneath (see BootloaderInfo.family). CMSIS_DAP carries the FB-RAT-DEV-011 research-spike caveat (docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §7) — its presence in this enum is a target-matrix placeholder, not a claim that CMSIS-DAP/OpenOCD support exists or is precedented on Android.

CatalogRef.description: FB-RAT-DEV-009: interoperate with Arduino CLI / PlatformIO board metadata, never own a separate board/package universe. UNCATALOGED is the honest fallback when neither toolchain's metadata recognizes this board — it is NOT a third catalog this constellation invents and grows over time.

catalogId.description: The catalog's own identifier for this board, e.g. an Arduino CLI FQBN ('arduino:avr:uno') or a PlatformIO board id ('esp32dev'). Null when catalogRef is UNCATALOGED, or when the catalog identifier has not yet been resolved.

displayName.description: Human-readable board name for display, e.g. 'Arduino Uno', 'ESP32-DevKitC-32', 'Raspberry Pi Pico'. Never used as identity — a renamed/relabeled board keeps the same deviceIdentityId.

vendorId.description: USB idVendor as a 4-hex-digit '0x'-prefixed string, e.g. '0x2341' (Arduino LLC).

supported.description: Whether this identity is known to have a bootloader entry path at all.

family.description: Which of the nine FB-RAT-DEV-010 families the bootloader itself speaks, when known — MAY differ from the outer DeviceIdentity.family (e.g. outer family CDC, bootloader family STK500, for a classic Arduino AVR board reached over a CDC-presenting USB-serial adapter).

entryMethod.description: Free-text description of how the bootloader is entered, e.g. '1200-baud touch auto-reset', 'BOOTSEL button held at power-on', 'double-tap reset'. Free text because entry methods are genuinely board-specific and not worth a closed vocabulary.

level.description: FB-RAT-DEV-004: flash preflight validates board identity confidence before erase. CONFIRMED: an exact USB VID/PID + protocol handshake match against known board metadata, or explicit user confirmation. PROBABLE: a VID/PID match against a device family that maps to more than one possible board (e.g. a generic CH340 clone matching many AVR boards). UNCERTAIN: heuristic-only (e.g. port-name guess, no successful protocol probe yet). UNKNOWN: no classification attempt has succeeded yet. A DeviceOperation's `preconditions.identityConfidenceAtLeast` gate (schemas/devices/operation.schema.json) is evaluated against this ordered scale — see docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §4 step 3.

basis.description: Free-text reasons supporting `level`, e.g. 'USB VID/PID exact match against arduino:avr:uno', 'STK500 protocol handshake succeeded', 'user manually selected board from list'. MAY be empty for level=UNKNOWN.
